column1: # The directory trees the QA gates must not gate on, one source for every reader: the Go
# discovery, patterns and qa-changed (src-go/qa/discovery, qa/patterns, qa/changed). A hand edit
# to one reader would be invisible to the others, so there is only this file.
#   list  shell: shell, YAML, JavaScript and Markdown discovery. python: Python discovery.
#   dir   a directory, or one file, matched as a whole /<dir>/ segment sequence anywhere in the
#         path, not only at the repository root.
# Daemon-deployed files are excluded, never gated here (owner's decision, 2026-11-09): the hooks
#   daemon ships and rewrites them on every upgrade, its own QA is their gate, and a finding in
#   one is reported upstream and never blocks this repository. They are .claude/ccy (with
#   CLAUDE/Plan/mkplan.bash and CLAUDE/core. The project handlers under .claude/hooks/handlers
#   are ours, so the python list does not exclude .claude/hooks. The secret and private-name
#   scans do not read this table and still cover every one of them.
# .git, .ansible: the WHOLE .ansible tree, not just roles/. It is gitignored Galaxy output and
#   `ansible-galaxy collection install` populates .ansible/collections/ with thousands of
#   third-party files carrying their own lint findings. Gating them made QA non-idempotent: a
#   repo that passed the first run failed the second, on vendored upstream fixtures.
# .claude/hooks-daemon-backups: the upgrade keeps the previous copy of any daemon-deployed tree
#   it replaces; it is a byte copy of .claude/skills, already excluded, and is recreated by
#   every upgrade, so deleting the directory defers the failure rather than fixing it.
# .claude/ccy: the whole CCY runtime tree (snapshots, plugins, history, saved transcripts) and
#   the daemon-deployed claude-supervise.py, for both lists.
# .claude/hooks: for shell only, the hook scripts the daemon generates (one per event, plus
# .claude/worktrees: checkouts of other branches, gated on their own branch.
# src-go/vendor: third-party Go modules exactly as `go mod vendor` writes them (Plan 00204), with
#   their own shell scripts, YAML and READMEs; judged whole by qa-go-deps (the vendor tree must be
#   byte for byte what go.mod and go.sum describe) and qa-go-vuln, never edited, so never linted.
# .semgrep: annotated rule FIXTURES, deliberately full of the broken patterns the rules must
#   catch; validated by the rule self-test in qa-patterns.bash, which is the check that belongs to it.
